0-scaffold.notes: ARCHITECTURE.md contract, tools/serve.mjs, tools/test.mjs, package.json, CI workflow, index.html, styles.css

1-foundations.notes: All four foundation modules delivered, 287 tests passing, zero failures, every self-score above the 8.5 threshold. Verified in Node and in real headless Chrome.

openIssues: FrameStats.droppedFrames is an estimate from frame intervals relative to the sim rate; on a 30 Hz display it reports one dropped frame per frame by design.
stepOnce() does not feed the statistics window, so stats() stays empty in a purely headless stepOnce-driven run.
Default vsync snapping (0.4 ms) makes the sim run ~0.1% slower than wall clock on a 59.94 Hz display; deliberate, disable with vsyncSnapMs: 0.
Allocation-free guarantees are asserted via V8's gc hook; those three tests silently skip if CI runs Node without it.
contractDeviations: types.js splits multi-@property lines one per line (TS JSDoc parser honours one per line); shapes otherwise verbatim.
types.js adds aliases RunStats / BestScore / Derived and mirrors Action, RenderView, Flash.
createLoop accepts optional injectables {now, raf, caf, doc} plus vsyncSnapMs and onError; defaults unchanged.
Loop adds suspended, hz, stepDt, resetStats(); FrameStats adds samples and skippedSteps.
Rng adds u32(), chance(p), saveState(out?), restoreState(words); state() is a uint32 fingerprint of the 128-bit state.
math.js adds TAU, HALF_PI, clamp01, invLerp, angleDiff, damp, dist, mod.
pool.js returns {items, count, capacity, free, acquire, release, releaseAt, retain, clear}; reset runs on release.
log.js adds setDebug, isDebug, clearErrors, installGlobalErrorCapture; errors is the exported live ring buffer (cap 64).

openIssues: No escape hatch from the 'loading' phase: pause and toTitle are ignored there. Needs ARCHITECTURE.md to add loading --toTitle--> title if Esc should work during a long build.
No TypeScript dependency, so JSDoc types are hand-verified; a tsc --checkJs gate would need GameState to gain an @property {Object} sim line.
Analogue stick turn gets the same 18/s ease as a keyboard key; may want an input-side analogue flag.
levelParams' size-based fuel floor dominates maze/populate's path-based budget at every level (deliberate, but a design decision to revisit).
tools/test.mjs parses '^# pass N' but node:test prints 'i pass N', so per-file tally counts are missing (exit codes correct).
contractDeviations: Additive GameState.sim block (SimScratch) for determinism; structurally still a GameState.
levelParams() returns four extra fields (fuelBase, fuelPerCell, fuelPerPathTile, cells).
Events cleared at the start of EVERY dispatch, not only on tick (strict superset of the contract).
save.js functions take an optional trailing storage parameter for test injection.
Phase-machine edges pinned: newGame from title|gameOver|levelComplete|paused only; toTitle from gameOver|levelComplete|paused only.
derived.exitDist is Infinity when no level is loaded; derived.nearExit is 0 there.
run.gemsTotal counts gems on the current level, not the whole run.
run.bestCombo is a summary statistic only and never multiplies score.
Oil flask is left on the floor when the tank is within 1 s of full.
levelData and explored are preserved during 'loading' and swapped atomically by levelReady.
sim.js exports more helpers than §4.2 names (moveCircle, hasLineOfSight, solidAt, setPhase, completeLevel, endRun, recordBest, ...).

openIssues: Mouse look requires pointer lock or a held left-drag; if a browser refuses pointer lock there is no on-screen prompt (belongs to src/ui).
navigator.getGamepads() allocates a fresh array per poll while a pad is connected; unavoidable through the standard API.
Touch (0.0038 rad/px) and mouse (0.0024 rad/px) look sensitivities were tuned by feel, not playtested against the finished raycaster.
The virtual stick's 40% zone is measured against the canvas rect, so an ultra-wide landscape phone gives a very wide stick zone.
Gamepad rumble is not implemented (not in the contract).
contractDeviations: opts is a superset of {sensitivity, invertLook}: also shouldLockPointer, touchRoot, touchOverlay, env. All optional.
Input adds updateOverlay(state) and a pointerLocked getter; isTouch is an accessor (touch detected lazily).
createTouchOverlay takes {onAction, document} and returns {update, setStick, destroy, element}.
input.js owns the touch overlay (created lazily on first touch); main.js can opt out with {touchOverlay:false}.
Gamepad right-stick yaw feeds frame.turn rather than frame.lookDX (the only dt-correct option).
Settings.invertLook is applied to yaw (mouse + touch look).
bindings.js exports lookup tables, gamepad tables, deadzone helpers and CONTROL_HINTS beyond 'the default key map'.
src/input/fake-dom.test-util.mjs is a test-only DOM double inside the module folder.

openIssues: Wall-torch light has no line-of-sight test around outside corners; a torch just around a convex corner spills slightly onto the adjacent corridor.
The first rendered frame costs ~40 ms in a cold browser (JIT warm-up) against ~1.2 ms steady state.
Wall variety is four painted variants plus a per-tile offset; repeats are visible in a big room.
The scanline overlay covers the whole viewport, including the black bars of a letterboxed portrait layout.
tools/test.mjs reports a duration instead of per-file pass counts (same note as core; exit codes correct).
contractDeviations: Palette is 66 entries, not ~32; the hard limit that matters (<=256) is asserted by a test.
createTextures returns an ARRAY for every field including floor (3) and ceiling (2).
createRaycaster takes an optional {textures, seed}; the returned object adds particles, textures, setTextures, depth(), dispose(); stats() is a superset of {ms}.
createPost returns {set, resize, destroy}; resize(cssW, cssH, internalH) is additive and required for correct scanlines; set() also accepts iris.
Shading uses a Doom-style COLORMAP (64 levels x 256 entries) rather than per-channel shade LUTs.
particles.js exports createParticles() (a pooled system) rather than a bare drawParticles(); RenderView shape is unchanged.
The head-bob/shake horizon is quantised to whole pixels to avoid a shimmering seam at the wall base.

core: Wiring: const loop = createLoop({ step, render }) — step(dt) always gets exactly 1/60 s; render(alpha, frameDt) gives alpha in [0,1) for interpolating px/py/pangle. loop.stats() returns a REUSED object.
window.__game.errors = errors (from core/log.js); call installGlobalErrorCapture() once at boot. window.__game.stepOnce = loop.stepOnce and window.__game.stats = loop.stats match the contract.
The loop auto-pauses on document.hidden and resumes without replaying hidden time; loop.running stays true, loop.suspended says why.
Deterministic seeding: const rng = createRng(state.seed) then rng.fork('maze'), rng.fork('items'), rng.fork('textures'). randomSeed() produces a fresh run seed.
hash2(x, y, seed) is the per-pixel/per-tile noise primitive for renderer/textures.js.
The rng golden values are pinned by a test: if the generator changes, bump the amaze.v1 persistence key.
tools/test.mjs's '^# pass N' regex does not match node:test's 'i pass N'; a one-character tweak restores the per-file counts.
Browser smoke check: logs/core-smoke.html + logs/core-smoke.mjs (gitignored scratch), node logs/core-smoke.mjs exits non-zero on failure.
state: EVENT ROUTING (can silently lose data): route state.events from a store subscriber — store.subscribe((s) => routeEvents(s.events, s)) — NOT only after the tick dispatch.
BOOT: const {best, settings} = loadPersist(); const store = createStore(createInitialState(settings, best), reducer); then dispatch levelReady with a demo level while phase is 'title'.

LOADING: on entering 'loading', call mazeClient.build(levelParams(state.level), seedFor(state)) and dispatch {type:'levelReady', data}. Per-level seed: createRng(state.seed).fork('level' + state.level).u32().
PERSISTENCE: savePersist({best: state.best, settings: state.settings}) on the gameOver event and on any setSetting action.

RENDERER WIRING: x = lerp(px, x, alpha), angle = lerpAngle(pangle, angle, alpha); light = clamp01(run.fuel / run.fuelMax); derived.nearExit drives the portal hum, derived.lowFuel the red vignette. state.explored is the minimap fog array (ty*width+tx).
state.levelData.items[i].taken is the authoritative collected flag.
HEADLESS TOOLS: {type:'debugWin'} wins the current level while playing; the reducer is deterministic given (seed, level data, input sequence).
NEVER mutate state from outside src/state; all writes go through dispatch.

Verified end to end: logs/state-integration.mjs plays 12 real generated levels with an autopilot (zero wall penetration, every level completed); logs/state-browser.* runs the same in headless Chrome with zero console output.
MEASURED: ~0 bytes allocated per idle step over 1,000,000 steps; 0.31 us/step in Node, ~23 us/step in Chrome.
BALANCE: populate.js treats fuelSeconds and par as FLOORS; the shipped curve gives ~4.7x on level 1 settling to ~2.0-2.5x from level 6. Retune via FUEL.PER_CELL_START / PER_CELL_END / DECAY_LEVELS.
input: Wiring: createInput(document.getElementById('overlay'), { sensitivity, invertLook, shouldLockPointer: () => store.getState().phase === 'playing' }); in step(): dispatch {type:'tick', dt, input: input.poll()}; call input.updateOverlay(state) once per frame; input.setOptions on settings change; input.destroy() on teardown.
poll() returns THE SAME InputFrame and THE SAME pressed Set every call — copy anything you keep.
Pointer lock is requested on canvas click while shouldLockPointer() is true; input.requestPointerLock() is available for any other user gesture.
styles.css MUST keep #post, #touch { pointer-events: none; } or no click reaches #overlay and pointer lock plus the virtual stick die silently.
Escape is bound to BOTH 'back' and 'pause'; M and Tab both give 'map'; WASD and arrows also emit up/down/left/right. Disambiguate by phase.
Menu auto-repeat: keyboard at the OS rate, gamepad from our own timers (0.42 s delay, 0.11 s interval).
Verified in real headless Chrome (logs/input-smoke.*, screenshots logs/input-desktop.png and logs/input-mobile.png): keyboard, pointer lock, iPhone-emulated touch, zero console errors.
renderer: Wiring, in order: const rc = createRaycaster(#view); const post = createPost(#post). On every resize call BOTH rc.resize(w, h, dpr) then post.resize(w, h, rc.internalSize.h).
Per frame: build ONE reusable RenderView (never allocate per frame) with the interpolated player, then rc.render(view). view.time is the renderer's clock in seconds.
Then post.set({ scanlines, vignette, lowFuelPulse, flash, iris }); set() is cheap every frame. iris 1 = open, 0 = closed: 0->1 on level start, 1->0 on level complete.
Two flash paths: view.flash tints the 3-D framebuffer only; post.set({flash}) tints the whole page including the HUD. Pick one per event.
Pickup sparkles: rc.particles.burst(PARTICLE.SPARK, x, y, 0.4, 24, 2.4, 0.7, PARTICLE_COLORS.spark, rng.next). Torch embers and gem twinkles are emitted by the renderer itself.
Per-run textures are optional: rc.setTextures(createTextures(state.seed)) during 'loading' only, not mid-level.

ASPECT RATIO: internal height is pinned at 240 and width clamped 320..560, so outside ~1.33..2.33 the browser stretches the world. Add #view { object-fit: contain } to letterbox (portrait phones are the real case).
rc.stats() and rc.internalSize are REUSED objects. stats().msAvg is valid from the first frame — good for tools/verify.mjs assertions.
rc.depth() is the live per-column wall distance buffer; treat as read-only.
The renderer never throws: a boot-order bug shows as a blank screen rather than a dead page — check stats().frames.

2-generation.notes: Generator, validator, populate, level, worker and client delivered. 67 unit tests, 117,306 mazes validated with zero failures, stress clean.

openIssues: Oil flasks fall back onto the solution path for ~6% of placements when a stretch has no side passage within 3 tiles; asserted to stay >=85% off-path.
WALK_SPEED (3.2) and CORNER_FACTOR (1.18) are duplicated knowledge between src/state/balance.js and src/maze/populate.js, since §2 forbids the import.
No static type-check was run (no TypeScript dev dependency); tsc --noEmit --allowJs --checkJs over src/maze would be a worthwhile CI addition.
tools/test.mjs reports a duration instead of per-file pass counts (same note as core; exit codes correct).
validate-mazes.mjs hand-matches the §6 level curve rather than importing balance.js, deliberately; pointing it at balance.js once final would catch drift.
The 4096x4096 maximum was verified once by hand (12.5 s generate, 491 MB RSS) but is not automated; stress.mjs covers 2000x2000 plus a 1x4096 guard.
contractDeviations: populateLevel returns {items, torches, fuel, par} instead of {items, torches}; LevelData itself still matches §3 exactly.
params.fuelSeconds and params.par are treated as FLOORS on the derived path-based budget, not as the budget.
createMazeClient takes an optional options object (threshold, timeoutMs, mode, WorkerCtor); no-argument call behaves as specified.
MazeClient exposes extra read-only accessors mode() and pending().
Extra exports: fuelBudget, assertMazeValid, levelTransferList, handleMazeRequest, and the DIR_* / MAX_CELLS_PER_SIDE / WORKER_CELL_THRESHOLD / cellToTile / tileToCell constants.
DIRS is exported both as a frozen bundle and as individual typed arrays (Object.freeze throws on typed arrays).
Two Validation fields pinned: pathLength counts TILES inclusive of both endpoints; deadEnds counts FLOOR tiles with exactly one FLOOR neighbour.
validateMaze adds checks §4.4 does not list: thick-wall dimension invariant, odd-lattice start/exit, every logical cell carved.
A worker-reported build error is retried synchronously rather than rejected immediately.
generateMaze floors fractional cols/rows rather than throwing; NaN/Infinity/0/negative/>4096 throw RangeError.

notesForIntegrator: FUEL SEAM — needs a decision. balance.js levelParams() returns fuelSeconds ~96 s at L1 to ~535 s at L30; populate treats that as a floor, so a direct run burns only 18-31% of the torch instead of the designed 50-85%. Fix (a) balance.js passes fuelSeconds: 0 / par: 0 and lets the maze module derive both (recommended), or (b) balance.js imports fuelBudget(pathLength, params) and scales it. LevelData.fuel is the authoritative number for run.fuel/run.fuelMax.

Wiring: const client = createMazeClient(); const data = await client.build(levelParams(level), seed); store.dispatch({type:'levelReady', data}). build() never throws synchronously and never rejects for infrastructure reasons. client.dispose() on teardown.
Worker packaging: src/maze/worker.js must be served from the same directory as client.js (new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url), {type:'module'}). No bundling. Verified in real headless Chrome.
Transfer semantics: the worker transfers maze.tiles.buffer and validation.path.buffer; the received LevelData owns them. Call levelTransferList() again before posting it onward.
Renderer/state may import src/maze/constants.js for TILE and DIR_DX/DIR_DY/DIR_OPPOSITE (same numbering as Torch.face, 0=E,1=S,2=W,3=N, y down).
Item coordinates are tile CENTRES (tx+0.5, ty+0.5); torch x/y are the WALL tile with face pointing at the lit corridor.
Sizes: levels <=40x40 build in well under 2 ms, so the 400-cell threshold means levels 1-2 build inline and the rest go async. Level 1 gives ~5 items, ~5 torches, ~40 s of fuel.
Scratch browser check: logs/maze-worker-check.html + logs/maze-worker-check.mjs (gitignored); worth folding into tools/verify.mjs.

3-hud-polish.notes: Wave 3 delivered: src/ui font/format/hud/menus plus the WebAudio synth in audio.js. 87 tests passing, zero failures; both modules self-scored 8.8, above the 8.5 threshold. Verified in real headless Chrome (screenshots, pointer/keyboard interaction, offline audio renders).

openIssues: Touch exercised only through synthetic pointer events in headless Chrome; no real-device test. Menu rows are >=50% of screen width and slider tracks padded by 2 units, so targets should be thumb-sized; the HUD itself has no tap targets.
The gothic display face is a heavy serif with blackletter cues rather than true blackletter, which is illegible at a 10-pixel cap height.
Screen transitions are a 0.26 s fade plus panel rise; the iris wipe named in S1 belongs to renderer/post.js and no menu hook exists in the contract.
Credits copy and the v0.1 footer are hard-coded in menus.js (CREDITS_LINES); both need editing at release.
The level-complete tally shows a gem row even at zero gems; unreachable in practice since populate.js always places GEM_MIN=4.
Roughly a dozen short-lived strings allocated per frame by the format.* calls in hud.js drawFuelGauge/drawScorePanel/drawDepthPanel; glyph, panel and minimap paths are allocation-free.
contractDeviations: src/ui may not import src/state (S2), so three sets of numbers are mirrored locally and must be kept in step with balance.js: menus.js SCORE_RULES (GEM_BASE 100, CLEAR_BASE 500, FUEL_UNIT 10, cross-checked against run.levelScore), menus.js OPTION_ITEMS slider ranges/steps mirroring SETTING_SPEC, and hud.js LOW_FUEL_FRACTION 0.2 mirroring FUEL.LOW_FRACTION.

S4.6 signatures are supersets, not changes: createHud(overlayCanvas, options?) also returns {surface, pop, reset, dispose}; createMenus(...) also returns {resize, surface, screen, dispose}; resize takes an optional third dpr argument (defaults to 1).
size in drawText/measureText options is an INTEGER PIXEL SCALE (1 = one font pixel per surface pixel), not a point size; scale is accepted as an alias.
measureText returns {width, height, lines} rather than a bare number.
Frame protocol: hud.render() clears the whole overlay and menus.render() does not, so the S4.7 order hud then menus is required. Calling either alone is safe.
menus.js imports hud.js: the shared overlay Surface and pixel-art primitives live there because S4.6 allows only four files in this folder. Intra-module, so the S2 dependency graph is unaffected.
The HUD derives score/gem/fuel pops from GameState deltas rather than state.events, so nothing is missed on a double-step frame or replayed on a double-render one.
The HUD face is a 5x7 design in an 8-row cell (one descender row) rather than a literal 5x7 grid; visible cap height is unchanged.

openIssues: Only the exit portal is spatialised (stereo pan by bearing); footsteps, pickups and bumps are deliberately non-positional, but wall torches have no audio counterpart yet.
The reverb is a damped feedback delay per bus, not a convolver, since an impulse response would mean a file and the zero-asset rule forbids it.
Voice stealing cuts a voice instantly rather than fading over ~5 ms; a click is theoretically possible under extreme overload, none measurable in the 60-event stress render.
The generative music RNG is seeded from options.seed (random by default), not the run seed, so a replayed seed does not reproduce the same ambience.
unlocked reports false against an OfflineAudioContext because its state stays suspended until startRendering(); harness-only.
Not verified with speakers: all mix judgements come from offline render measurements, so a human listening pass before release is still worth a minute.
contractDeviations: S4.6 createAudio() -> {unlock(), handle(events, state), setVolume(v, music), update(state)} is implemented with exactly those names and argument orders. ADDITIVE ONLY: an optional options object (injectable AudioContext factory, doc, volume, music, maxVoices, seed, autoUnlock) plus playUi(kind), suspend(), resume(), dispose(), stats() and the unlocked/available getters.

A frozen AUDIO tuning table is exported from audio.js. CLAUDE.md puts tuning numbers in src/state/balance.js, but S2 forbids src/ui importing src/state, so the synthesis constants live in audio.js; they are audio-internal, not gameplay balance.

update(state) also reads state.levelData.maze.exit and state.player.{x,y,angle,vx,vy} beyond the derived block the contract names: the portal pan needs the exit bearing and footstep intensity needs ground speed. All reads are read-only GameState fields.

update(state) adopts state.settings.volume/.music automatically whenever they change, so main.js need not call setVolume() after an options edit; an explicit setVolume() still wins until the slider moves.

ui: Wiring: const hud = createHud(overlayCanvas); const menus = createMenus(overlayCanvas, {onNewGame, onResume, onQuit, onNextLevel, onSetting, onUiSound}); on layout change call hud.resize(cssW, cssH, devicePixelRatio) AND menus.resize(...) (shared Surface, so the second is a cheap no-op); each frame hud.render(state, loop.stats(), alpha) then menus.render(state).

Do NOT set overlay.width/height yourself: the surface owns the backing store and sizes it to cssW x cssH x dpr (capped at ~4.2 MP). styles.css already stretches the canvas to 100%/100%, which the mapping assumes.

Input: if (!menus.handleInput(inputFrame, state)) { your pause/map/mute handling }. It returns false during playing and loading, true on every menu screen. Esc/back on pause calls onResume; on levelComplete/gameOver it calls onQuit.

Pointer: forward pointermove/pointerdown/pointerup/pointerleave to menus.handlePointer(ev) and preventDefault when it returns true; true also means do not request pointer lock for that click. Verified at devicePixelRatio 1 and 2 (logs/ui-interact.mjs).

Callbacks map straight to dispatches: onNewGame -> newGame with seed: randomSeed() (menus never invent a seed), onResume -> resume, onQuit -> toTitle, onNextLevel -> nextLevel, onSetting(key, value) -> setSetting. onUiSound carries uiMove|uiConfirm|uiBack|uiDeny; route the first two to the matching GameEvent for audio.js.
hud.reset() on newGame clears the score roll and minimap cache instantly; the HUD also self-resets whenever state.level changes.
HUD and menus take their clock from state.time (plus alpha/60 for the HUD), so animation stops cleanly with the sim and frozen-time screenshots are deterministic.

Debug: ?debug=1 (core/log.isDebug) adds the FPS line; pass loop.stats() as the second render argument or it prints NO FRAME STATS. The FrameStats object may be the loop reused instance; the HUD only reads it.
Everything degrades rather than throwing: a null canvas, a canvas with no 2-D context, a null or garbage state, a missing callback and a throwing callback are all covered by tests.

Verification artefacts: logs/release-{wide,phone}-*.png (all screens), logs/ship-{tablet,land,big,small}-*.png (extreme viewports), logs/ui-shot.mjs, logs/ui-interact.mjs (18 real-browser pointer/keyboard assertions at dpr 1 and 2), logs/ui-proof.mjs (ASCII glyph proof sheet). Whole overlay costs ~0.2 ms/frame at 1280x720 with zero console errors.

Preview harness: http://localhost:5173/src/ui/preview.html with ?screen=hud|title|options|credits|pause|loading|complete|gameover|font, ?t=SEC freeze, ?low=1, ?level=N, ?minimap=0, ?reduced=1, ?debug=1, ?hint=1; window.__ui exposes {state, hud, menus, setScreen, step, sfx, sfxCount}.
audio: Wiring: const audio = createAudio() once at boot; in step() audio.handle(state.events, state) after the tick dispatch; once per frame audio.update(state). update() is cheap and allocation-free when nothing moves.

unlock(): the module attaches its own one-shot pointerdown/keydown/touchend listeners to document and unlocks on the first gesture (autoUnlock:false to opt out). Calling audio.unlock() from your own gesture handler is safe and idempotent; no AudioContext is constructed before a gesture, so Chrome never prints the autoplay warning.
Hidden tab: suspends on visibilitychange and resumes on return, rebasing its scheduler clocks so a long background pause does not dump a backlog of sounds. The loop own pause is independent.
Menus: audio.playUi(move|confirm|back), or emit uiMove/uiConfirm GameEvents; both paths produce the same blips. The engine plays a back blip on entering paused and a confirm blip on resuming.

Volume/mute: setVolume(volume, music) mirrors Settings; setVolume(0) is a hard mute that allocates NO WebAudio nodes at all, so a mute hotkey is also a CPU saving. Dispatching setSetting volume 0 is picked up by update() on its own.
Teardown: audio.dispose() stops and disconnects every node, removes its listeners and closes the context; idempotent, and the object stays safely callable.
Debug: audio.stats() returns a reused object {voices, maxVoices, stolen, dropped, time, failures, state}; steadily growing stolen/dropped would mean maxVoices is too low.

Measured cue peaks with music muted (logs/audio-check.mjs, real OfflineAudioContext in headless Chrome): footstep walk 0.067 / sprint 0.098, bump 0.158, gem 0.252 (combo x4 0.468), oil 0.168, lowFuel 0.122, levelStart 0.310, levelComplete 0.325, gameOver 0.265, UI 0.109, portal-near 0.179, heartbeat 0.353, torch bed 0.025, music 0.073, muted exactly 0.0. A 60-event burst peaks at 0.6998, the tanh limiter mathematical ceiling, so the output can never clip.
Re-run verification any time with node logs/audio-check.mjs (needs the dev server); it reports peak/RMS/NaN/voice stats per cue and fails loudly if a cue goes silent or a scheduling call throws.

integration.notes: Integration complete: src/main.js composition root wires core/state/input/maze/renderer/ui/audio behind a guarded boot; index.html, styles.css, tools/verify.mjs autopilot and the CI quality gate delivered; ARCHITECTURE.md reconciled section by section with the shipped code. The game boots, plays, descends and ends with zero console output.
seamFixes: styles.css / layout (CRITICAL, found by running it): #overlay and #touch were absolutely positioned *replaced* elements with width:auto, so the canvas fell back to its 300x150 intrinsic size and the ENTIRE HUD and every menu rendered in a postage stamp in the top-left corner. Fixed with calc()-sized boxes; verify now asserts the overlay backing store matches the viewport.

index.html layer order (renderer ↔ ui): #post now sits BELOW #overlay, so the vignette/iris/flash frame the world and never darken the HUD or a menu panel. Without it the level-complete iris would have blacked out its own tally screen.

src/input/touch-overlay.js (input ↔ ui): the MAP/PAUSE bar and the HUD's score panel both claimed the top-right corner and overlapped on every touch device. One-line seam fix — the bar now carries class `amaze-touch-bar` (no behaviour change, documented in-file) — and styles.css pushes it below the HUD's top row.

src/main.js pauses on pointer-lock loss (input ↔ state): browsers give the pointer back on Escape WITHOUT delivering that keypress to the page, so the first Escape freed the cursor and left the game running behind it. Losing the lock while playing now dispatches pause.

Fuel budget (maze ↔ state, flagged by the maze builder as needing a decision): resolved in favour of balance.js's size-based floor and documented in ARCHITECTURE.md §4.4/§6. populate.js's path-derived curve leaves level 10 at ~1.2x the optimal route — unwinnable for a player who cannot see the maze; the shipped floor gives ~4x on level 1 and ~3x from level 6. Both stay in the code: populate keeps deriving (validate-mazes keeps proving feasibility), balance keeps raising.

Loading phase escape (state, flagged by the state builder): NOT changed in src/state. main.js owns recovery instead (build tokens, two reseeded retries, 12 s watchdog), keeping the phase machine total; documented in §4.2 so the next reader knows it is deliberate.

tools/test.mjs tally regex (reported independently by core, state, maze and renderer builders): parsed '^# pass N' but node:test's default reporter prints 'ℹ pass N', so the per-file column showed a duration. Now `^\D*pass (\d+)$` — 359 test counts are visible again.

HUD pop double-fire avoided: the HUD derives score/fuel pops from GameState deltas by design, so main.js deliberately does NOT also pop on pickup events (would show every gem twice). Documented in §4.6 and in main.js.

ARCHITECTURE.md reconciled with reality across §3 (GameState.sim, Validation.pathLength/deadEnds definitions, events cleared per dispatch), §4.1–§4.7 (every delivered signature), §5 (real gate thresholds) and §6 (new assumptions). 388 lines changed; every builder deviation is either adopted with its reason or marked an integrator decision.
openIssues: MEDIUM — Portrait phones letterbox to a 4:3 band (~35% of screen height). §4.5 pins the framebuffer at 240 rows with the width clamped to 320…560, so it can NEVER be taller than 4:3; cropping to fill would cut the horizontal FOV to a slit. Laid out as a handheld cabinet instead (gauges above, world, control deck below with the compass, minimap and virtual stick). A real fix needs a renderer change (variable internal height) — a contract change, not a seam repair.

MEDIUM — Difficulty plateaus after level ~18: the maze is capped at 40x40 cells and the fuel-per-cell rate has finished decaying, so levels 18+ differ only by braid and the score multiplier. Fine for an arcade loop, but a future pass should add a late-game pressure (shrinking base fuel, or braid past 0.25).
LOW — tools/verify.mjs needs a browser and the dev server, so CI gates on npm test + validate-mazes + stress only. A CI verify would need a Chrome action plus a background server step.

LOW — The autopilot steers with the real input path but scrapes corners, so its fuel figures are pessimistic (it cleared level 1 with 76/96 s left; a clean run leaves more). Screenshots now wait for a clear corridor before firing, which fixed the 'nose against a wall' shots.

integration.summary:
INTEGRATION COMPLETE — A-MAZE boots, plays, descends and ends with zero console output.

WIRED (src/main.js, 830 lines, guarded boot → styled fatal panel instead of a black page):
persist → store → raycaster(#view) → post(#post) → hud+menus(#overlay) → input(#overlay, touch into #touch) → audio → maze client → loop. step(dt) polls input once, offers the frame to menus.handleInput, falls through to composition-root hotkeys (pause/map/mute), then dispatches tick and advances a loading watchdog. render(alpha) mutates ONE RenderView (interpolated by lerp/lerpAngle), then raycaster → hud → menus → post → audio.update → input.updateOverlay; all per-frame objects (RenderView, post options, tick action) are reused. Events are routed from a store subscriber (not after the tick) because state.events is cleared at the top of every dispatch: audio.handle gets the array, pickups burst particles + tint the world, levelComplete/gameOver tint the page, phase changes start level builds and release pointer lock, gameOver/levelComplete/setSetting persist. Level requests carry a token (stale/late answers dropped), retry twice reseeded on genuine failure, and a 12 s watchdog rebuilds. Iris wipe closes for loading/complete/gameOver and opens on level start. Layout fits #view+#post to the framebuffer aspect, snapping to a whole pixel multiple when it costs <3% (exact 3x at 720p), centred — at 42% height in portrait where 240 rows must letterbox; #overlay/#touch are inset by safe areas. Auto-pause on blur, hidden tab AND pointer-lock loss. ?headless=1/?debug=1 expose window.__game {ready,state,dispatch,subscribe,stepOnce,stats,renderStats,audioStats,errors,input:{inject,clear}}; ?seed=N pins the run; ?fatal=1 shows the error screen.

ALSO: index.html (description, OG/Twitter cards, inline-SVG torch favicon, 10 modulepreloads, layer reorder to #view→#post→#overlay→#touch); styles.css (full-bleed, pixelated, safe areas, no scroll/overscroll, cursor hidden only while locked, focus-visible only, noscript panel); tools/verify.mjs (new, BFS-pathfinding autopilot through the real maze); CI quality gate; ARCHITECTURE.md reconciled section by section against the shipped code; CLAUDE.md commands/rules.

No skills were used — none in the available set (Godot/Blender/itch/artifact/design) applies to vanilla ES-module web-game integration. Skills that would have paid for themselves: (1) "headless-browser-module-check" wrapping the puppeteer-core + dev-server + window.__result harness that four builders and I each hand-rolled; (2) "js-typecheck-jsdoc" to run tsc --checkJs against a // @ts-check repo with no TypeScript dependency; (3) a "web-game-verify" skill with the fps/heap/console-gate patterns (CDP HeapProfiler.collectGarbage + Performance.getMetrics, vsync-on vs vsync-off fps) — I rebuilt all of it from scratch.

Laid out as a handheld cabinet instead (gauges above, world, control deck below with the compass, minimap and virtual stick). A real fix needs a renderer change (variable internal height) — a contract change, not a seam repair.

contractDeviations: styles.css / layout (CRITICAL, found by running it): #overlay and #touch were absolutely positioned *replaced* elements with width:auto, so the canvas fell back to its 300x150 intrinsic size and the ENTIRE HUD and every menu rendered in a postage stamp in the top-left corner. Fixed with calc()-sized boxes; verify now asserts the overlay backing store matches the viewport.

index.html layer order (renderer ↔ ui): #post now sits BELOW #overlay, so the vignette/iris/flash frame the world and never darken the HUD or a menu panel. Without it the level-complete iris would have blacked out its own tally screen.

src/input/touch-overlay.js (input ↔ ui): the MAP/PAUSE bar and the HUD's score panel both claimed the top-right corner and overlapped on every touch device. One-line seam fix — the bar now carries class `amaze-touch-bar` (no behaviour change, documented in-file) — and styles.css pushes it below the HUD's top row.

src/main.js pauses on pointer-lock loss (input ↔ state): browsers give the pointer back on Escape WITHOUT delivering that keypress to the page, so the first Escape freed the cursor and left the game running behind it. Losing the lock while playing now dispatches pause.

Fuel budget (maze ↔ state, flagged by the maze builder as needing a decision): resolved in favour of balance.js's size-based floor and documented in ARCHITECTURE.md §4.4/§6. populate.js's path-derived curve leaves level 10 at ~1.2x the optimal route — unwinnable for a player who cannot see the maze; the shipped floor gives ~4x on level 1 and ~3x from level 6. Both stay in the code: populate keeps deriving (validate-mazes keeps proving feasibility), balance keeps raising.

Loading phase escape (state, flagged by the state builder): NOT changed in src/state. main.js owns recovery instead (build tokens, two reseeded retries, 12 s watchdog), keeping the phase machine total; documented in §4.2 so the next reader knows it is deliberate.

tools/test.mjs tally regex (reported independently by core, state, maze and renderer builders): parsed '^# pass N' but node:test's default reporter prints 'ℹ pass N', so the per-file column showed a duration. Now `^\D*pass (\d+)$` — 359 test counts are visible again.

HUD pop double-fire avoided: the HUD derives score/fuel pops from GameState deltas by design, so main.js deliberately does NOT also pop on pickup events (would show every gem twice). Documented in §4.6 and in main.js.

ARCHITECTURE.md reconciled with reality across §3 (GameState.sim, Validation.pathLength/deadEnds definitions, events cleared per dispatch), §4.1–§4.7 (every delivered signature), §5 (real gate thresholds) and §6 (new assumptions). 388 lines changed; every builder deviation is either adopted with its reason or marked an integrator decision.

integration: Boot: src/main.js is the only composition root. persist -> store -> raycaster(#view) -> post(#post) -> hud+menus(#overlay) -> input(#overlay, touch into #touch) -> audio -> maze client -> loop. Boot is guarded; a failure shows a styled fatal panel instead of a black page (?fatal=1 to see it).
Events are routed from a store subscriber, NOT after the tick, because state.events is cleared at the top of every dispatch.
render(alpha) mutates ONE reused RenderView, then raycaster -> hud -> menus -> post -> audio.update -> input.updateOverlay. The hud/menus order is required; no per-frame allocation.
Level builds carry a token (stale answers dropped), retry twice reseeded on genuine failure, and a 12 s watchdog rebuilds. Recovery lives in main.js, not in the phase machine.

The HUD derives score/fuel pops from GameState deltas, so main.js deliberately does NOT also pop on pickup events (it would double-count every gem).

5-massive-mazes.notes: MASSIVE MAZES + the refillable torch economy. Level 1 is 16x16 cells (33x33 tiles) growing +8 cells/side to a 128x128-cell cap (257x257 tiles, 16,384 cells) at level 15; past the cap levels get harder, not bigger. The torch is a 110-150 s TANK independent of maze area and oil flasks are the economy, with a placement guarantee that the solution path never contains a fuel desert. Every per-frame and per-step cost was re-cut to be independent of maze size: a bucket grid for pickups, a spatial index for sprites and lights, an incremental raster for the new three-state map.
seamFixes: settings.mapMode (state <-> ui): the UI shipped a three-state map (off/corner/full) but src/state had only the legacy `minimap` boolean, so FULL could not survive a reload and the M key only reached two states. SETTING_SPEC gained a third kind, `enum`, plus settings.mapMode; coerceSetting takes only a listed value and ignores anything else rather than snapping to the default. `minimap` is kept as the legacy mirror and main.js writes both.

src/main.js map hotkey: replaced the `minimap` toggle with hud.cycleMap() + both setSettings, which is what makes the FULL map reachable in the shipped game at all. The touch MAP button emits the same action, so it gets all three states for free.

run.refuels / run.distance (state <-> ui): the HUD tank tally and the level-complete / game-over expedition strip were written against fields that did not exist. Added in src/state: refuels per LEVEL (reset by levelReady), distance per RUN (reset by newGame, measured after collision so wall-scraping cannot inflate it).

src/main.js level install: a completed build is now queued and dispatched from step() after MIN_LOAD_S (0.8 s). A 128x128 level comes back in ~25-60 ms, so the loading screen used to exist for three frames - the iris started its wipe and snapped back open and the banner naming the labyrinth was never readable. It is a floor on the loading phase, not a delay added to a slow build, and the watchdog/stale-token/retry paths all go through it.
src/main.js DEMO_LEVEL 3 -> 1: the title maze is now 16x16 cells, under the maze client 400-cell worker threshold, so the title costs no worker spin-up at boot and carries the smallest sprite load.
tools/verify.mjs wall-clock budgets: LEVEL1/LEVEL2 were 60 s/45 s against a level 1 that now takes the autopilot ~115 s. Raised to 400/500 and the gate extended to the size cap.

supersedes: integration: 'Difficulty plateaus after level ~18: the maze is capped at 40x40 cells and the fuel-per-cell rate has finished decaying' — the cap is now 128x128 at level 15 and past it braid, drain and oil density keep moving, which is exactly the late-game pressure that issue asked for.
integration/maze: the fuel seam ('balance.js supplies a size-based floor that always wins over populate's path-derived budget') — there is one owner of the tank now and no floor to win.

4-massive-mazes.notes: MASSIVE MAZES + refillable torch economy. Fuel is a TANK (110 s at L1 -> 150 s at the cap) independent of maze area; oil flasks are the economy (35% of tank each, clamped 25-60 s, 7-22 refuels per level). Measured finding that reshaped the design: the ~13-tiles-per-cell-side path law only holds for BRAIDED mazes (a perfect maze's farthest route is ~side^1.6: 72x72 at braid 0 = 3,903 path tiles vs 907 at braid 0.25), so the braid ramp was front-loaded to keep the curve monotone at 3.6 -> 13.5 minutes. Per-step cost made size-independent: a CSR 4-tile bucket grid for pickups (0.675 us/step on a 128x128/819-item level vs 0.635 us on the old 6x6, ratio 1.06x), pooled explored buffer, fixed 7x7 LOS window. Feasibility proven on 250 real levels (levels 1-25 x 10 seeds) with a 2.0x-wander autopilot: 250/250 reached the exit, lowest fuel 62-70% of tank, with a flask-stripped negative control that correctly dies.
4-massive-mazes.sizeCurve: L1 16x16 cells / 33x33 tiles; +8 cells/side/level; cap 128x128 cells / 257x257 tiles / 16,384 cells at L15 (CAP_LEVEL derived from BASE_CELLS 16, GROWTH 8, MAX_CELLS 128). Braid 0 -> 0.6 over 17 levels, square-root shaped (0.54 at L15, 0.6 from L18); past the cap drain +2%/level to 1.35x and oil density thins 1/20 -> 1/30 cells.

openIssues: FUEL.LOW_FRACTION left at 0.2 so the src/ui/hud.js mirror does not drift; on the new tank that is a 22-30 s warning and must be changed in both files together if the ui owner wants longer.

The pinned score formulas were not touched, so the clear bonus is now roughly constant per level (~1500 x level) while gems scale with area (6 at L1 -> 273 at the cap): the incentive tips from 'get out fast' to 'explore'. A pacing change the lead should sign off.

src/state/perf.test.mjs and feasibility.test.mjs import src/maze as a TEST-ONLY dependency; the section 2 runtime rule is unchanged but the gate list in section 5 must say so.

Level 1 is 16x16 cells growing +8 cells/side to a 128x128-cell cap (257x257 tiles, 819 items) at level 15; the torch became a 110-150 s tank refilled from oil flasks instead of a whole-level budget, with the braid ramp front-loaded after measuring that a perfect maze's farthest route is superlinear (~side^1.6) and would have made levels 3-8 longer than level 15. Step cost is now size-independent (1.06x from the smallest level to the largest, via a CSR bucket grid for pickups) and 108,000 ticks on a cap-size level grow the heap by 5.4 KiB. src/state: 110 tests passing, 0 failing, self-score 9; repo 503 tests, validate-mazes and stress clean; the browser run descends to the cap and soaks it for 60.01 s at 623.4 fps with a 19.3 ms worst build frame gap and zero console output. openIssues: populate.js and feasibility.test.mjs measure the oil gap with slightly different reachability definitions, so they report numbers a few tiles apart. Both pass their own (stricter) bound and the campaign has a 70% torch reserve at its worst point, but the two should be reconciled so validate-mazes and feasibility.test.mjs report the same figure.

LEVEL.PATH_TILES_PER_SIDE = 13 overestimates the shipped route at the deepest braid (~7.1 measured). It feeds only the par FLOOR, which populate.js overrides with the real path, so nothing is wrong today - but the constant reads stale.

gatherLights still picks the nearest 8 torches. At the new density (~1300 on level 15) more than 8 sconces can be within lighting range in a braided junction. MAX_LIGHTS is the knob and the ring search makes 12 or 16 nearly free.
